## Work performed

Current public/repository evidence does not establish a new crawlability, canonical, `hreflang`, structured-data, redirect, broken-link, rendering, accessibility, persistent-performance, or deployment defect. The repository already generates canonical and language-alternate metadata, Article structured data, sitemap entries, and static audit artifacts. An unrelated technical SEO change would therefore be speculation, so today's implementation is limited to the Daily Report and navigation/operating-state records.

Before today's publication, the newest ten actually published Daily Reports are **7 eBPF-centered / 1 pure Agent / 2 adjacent systems**. The report rotating out is the eBPF-centered `2026-09-06` architecture-specialization report. Today's report is eBPF-centered, so the resulting newest-ten mix remains **7 / 1 / 2**.

The active roadmap remains **eBPF Deployment Compatibility and Lifecycle**, but two strong remaining boundaries already exist as open, unmerged attempts: PR `#208` covers evolving kernel-interface negotiation and PR `#207` covers pinned-state durability. They are not published state and are not counted in the mix. A reproducible capability-manifest topic also risks collapsing back into the already published September 15 admission-receipt boundary.

A fresh material external development provides a stronger distinct report today. On September 16, a 20-patch `bpf-next` series proposed running compiler-generated exception cleanup landing pads while `bpf_throw()` unwinds. LLVM 23 already contains the compiler-side `.bpf_cleanup` support. The kernel proposal spans verifier control flow, resource tracking, libbpf loading/linking, x86-64 and arm64 JIT dispatch, and selftests.

Selected report: **“Can eBPF Exceptions Unwind Resources Safely?” / “eBPF 异常展开时，能安全释放资源吗？”**. Its unresolved mechanism is cross-layer cleanup correctness: compiler region metadata, libbpf transformation, verifier cleanup state, and runtime/JIT PC dispatch must all describe the same unwind transition. The report develops an explicit cleanup-effect discipline, an auditable artifact descriptor, and a cross-JIT differential unwind harness. It treats the kernel work as under review and the Rust BPF exception toolchain as incomplete rather than claiming a current production ABI.

No raw analytics, credentials, private source identifiers, or personal information are added to Git. The pinned SEO skill remains unchanged.
